summary: This round-3 change closes two real, previously-identified gaps in the dispatch-time DDL authorization gate: it widens keyword coverage to privilege-escalation DCL/DDL primitives (GRANT, REVOKE, CREATE/ALTER/DROP ROLE, CREATE/ALTER/DROP USER, SECURITY DEFINER, REASSIGN OWNED) that previously passed through undetected, and it replaces the shape-only PRE-APPROVED-LIVE-DDL citation check with a real existence check (a cited KE-<date>-<time>-<hex> ID must appear literally somewhere under ai-os/, and an OWNER_DECISIONS_NEEDED_<date>.yaml reference must name a file that actually exists on disk), so a fabricated-but-well-formed citation like KE-20260726-999999-dead is now correctly rejected instead of accepted on regex shape alone. The integration into task-gateway.py's cmd_start() follows the exact existing run()/json.loads()/fail() pattern used by tight_task_validation.py, fails closed on unparseable output, and sits before veridian-task.py create as intended. All 28 new tests pass, the module compiles cleanly, the modified YAML parses, and the cited fixture files (KE-20260725-061008-8423, OWNER_DECISIONS_NEEDED_2026-07-23.yaml) were independently confirmed to exist on disk rather than trusting the self-report. The diff does not touch .github/workflows/** or any tier2-triggering path (migrations/, schema.*, auth/, *.sql, permission/payment/billing/rls/security in path), consistent with its tier1 pre-classification. Residual limitations are honestly documented rather than hidden: this remains a dispatch-time prompt-text scan (not a runtime MCP tool-call interceptor), the existence check proves a cited record is real but not that it semantically approves this specific DDL action, and the dated-free-text-note approval path remains format-only with no existence check -- none of these are new regressions, all are explicitly called out in the module docstring as known, accepted gaps.
issues: Minor: the PRE-APPROVED-LIVE-DDL: marker regex (APPROVAL_LINE_RE) is case-sensitive while DDL keyword matching is case-insensitive -- a lowercase marker fails to be recognized and the prompt is rejected (fails closed, not a bypass, but an inconsistency worth normalizing later).

Minor: KE-id existence check only requires the matched ID substring to appear literally somewhere under ai-os/, not that the surrounding reference text is otherwise meaningful -- a real KE id pasted alongside irrelevant text still passes. This is explicitly documented as an accepted limitation (existence != semantic relevance to this specific action), not a new gap introduced by this change.

Minor: bare GRANT/REVOKE keyword matching will also trigger on ordinary English prose using those words (e.g. 'grant read access' in a SCOPE description), causing over-blocking/false-positive citation demands rather than under-blocking -- an acceptable fail-closed trade-off for a security gate but may cause some avoidable friction on legitimate non-SQL prompts.
